title: Choosing a function type for a model
body: Match the function type to the pattern in the data or context, in the order the CED lists them.

items.label: Linear
items.meaning: Data or contexts that demonstrate roughly constant rates of change (1.13.A.1).

items.label: Quadratic
items.meaning: Data or contexts with roughly linear rates of change, or roughly symmetric data with a unique maximum or minimum value (1.13.A.2). Geometric contexts involving area or two dimensions can often be modeled by quadratic functions (1.13.A.3).

items.label: Cubic
items.meaning: Geometric contexts involving volume or three dimensions can often be modeled by cubic functions (1.13.A.3).

items.label: Polynomial
items.meaning: Data or contexts with multiple real zeros or multiple maxima or minima (1.13.A.4).

items.label: Polynomial of degree n
items.meaning: Data or contexts that demonstrate roughly constant nonzero nth differences (1.13.A.5).

items.label: Piecewise-defined
items.meaning: A set of functions defined over nonoverlapping domain intervals, useful when a data set or scenario demonstrates different characteristics over different intervals (1.13.A.7).

ced_evidence: 1.13.A.1–1.13.A.7: "Linear functions model data sets or aspects of contextual scenarios that demonstrate roughly constant rates of change."
